body.statement: For sample sizes in the deterministic eventual regime \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), uniformly over the instrumental strengthened subclass \(P\in\mathcal M\), the quantitative condition \(\mathsf G_n\) yields \(\{S_n(\theta)-S_n^{\circ}\}/a(T_n(P))\to0\) in probability. The oracle statistic admits a coupling with \(\{S_n^{\circ}-M_{T_n(P)}\}/a(T_n(P))\to0\), with common constrained and unconstrained contact localization, locally frozen coefficients glued by \(T_n(P)\), and an asymptotically equivalent maximum over the two one-sided limits in each empirical dose cell. Consequently, uniformly for \(x\) in compact sets, \(\Pr_P\{[S_n(\theta)-b(T_n(P))]/a(T_n(P))\le x\}\to\exp\{-e^{-x}\}\). At one fixed dose the construction recovers Doss's (2026) pointwise LR limit, while the continuum coupling and eventual-regime Gumbel law strictly strengthen that fixed-dose result on \(\mathcal M\).
body.justification: The canonical theorem becomes simultaneous observed-law inference only after the displayed Gumbel-scale threshold is verified and the actual optimized cross-fitted statistic is transferred on the instrumental smooth subclass. The historical node id does not assert an exact-dose causal interpretation.
body.gap: Doss (2026) proves a fixed-dose LR limit under pointwise remainder conditions, while Westling and Carone (2020) prove pointwise primitive transfer; neither controls a continuum maximum at its moving threshold or asserts the global fixed-radius subclass used here.
body.consumer: The spatial clock is justified algebraically, but the continuum LR statistic has not been coupled to the canonical growing-domain maximum.

obligation.what_is_open: A measurable uniform coupling of the growing-domain oracle continuum LR statistic to the canonical maximum, followed by optimized stability for the cross-fitted statistic, remains unavailable.
obligation.obstruction: The claim requires a sorted-residual strong approximation, interpolation of rank and variance clocks, common constrained and unconstrained contact localization, local coefficient freezing with overlap gluing, and empirical dose-cell comparison at a moving logarithmic threshold.
obligation.attempted: The exact local cube-root scale was derived, all required divisions were justified from overlap, slope, and variance bounds, and its inverse was integrated to obtain the stated spatial-volume clock exactly. A global quadratic approximation cannot replace the missing local gluing argument.
obligation.partial_result:
For \(a\in J\), define the local dose scale
\[
 h_n(a)=\left\{\frac{4\kappa(a)}{n f(a)\theta'(a)^2}\right\}^{1/3}.
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:p-normalization}\) and \(\texttt{ass:overlap}\),
\[
 c_g\le f(a)=\int g(a\mid w)p(w)\,dw\le C_g.
\]
Together with \(\texttt{ass:strict-slope}\) and \(\texttt{ass:variance}\), this makes \(h_n(a)\) positive and gives constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on the fixed model constants, such that
\[
 c\le n^{1/3}h_n(a)\le C
\]
uniformly in \(a\in J\) and \(P\in\mathcal M\).  Direct algebra gives
\[
 \frac1{h_n(a)}
 =n^{1/3}\left\{\frac{f(a)\theta'(a)^2}{4\kappa(a)}\right\}^{1/3}
\]
and therefore
\[
 \int_J\frac{da}{h_n(a)}
 =n^{1/3}\int_J
   \left\{\frac{f(a)\theta'(a)^2}{4\kappa(a)}\right\}^{1/3}da
 =T_n(P).
\]
Consequently
\[
 a\longmapsto\int_{\inf J}^{a}h_n(v)^{-1}\,dv
\]
is a bi-Lipschitz canonical coordinate that maps \(J\) to an interval of length exactly \(T_n(P)\).  This proves the spatial-volume clock and all divisions used in it.  It does not construct the claimed coupling: that requires a sorted-residual strong approximation, interpolation of the empirical rank and variance clocks, common contact localization for both optimized problems, locally uniform coefficient freezing with overlap gluing, and comparison of both one-sided limits in every empirical dose cell at a threshold of order \(\log n\).
